title: The business of belonging — Extension 6

outcome.canDo: I can evaluate how brands create communities and argue for or against company investment in community-building using evaluative language and rhetorical questions. Apply the choice to a new B2 context.

outcome.scenario: You are asked to advise the marketing director of a mid-sized apparel brand. After reading a feature on how brands buy loyalty, write a short proposal evaluating two community-building strategies and recommending one, acknowledging potential risks.
outcome.scenarioArabic: طُلب منك تقديم مشورة لمدير التسويق في علامة أزياء متوسطة. بعد قراءة تقرير حول كيف تشتري العلامات التجارية الولاء، اكتب اقتراحًا قصيرًا يقيم استراتيجيتين لبناء المجتمع ويوصي بإحداهما مع الاعتراف بالمخاطر المحتملة.

retrieval.prompt: Write a 120-word paragraph that clearly states your viewpoint on whether corporate-led communities are authentic. Use at least two evaluative expressions (e.g. arguably, problematic) and one rhetorical question to engage the reader. Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.

retrieval.prompt: Summarise two pieces of evidence (one consumer quote, one statistic) from the reading in two sentences and explain briefly which is stronger and why, using comparative evaluative language (e.g. more compelling, less reliable). Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Move from listing evidence to weighing its strength using B2 evaluative vocabulary.

retrieval.prompt: Write three sentences outlining two likely consequences if the brand prioritises short-term promotions over community-building, using consequence markers (therefore, as a result). Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Extend the B1 idea of stating consequences into richer, signposted reasoning.

retrieval.prompt: Draft a short 80–100 word negotiation message from marketing to finance proposing a modest budget for community events, acknowledging a counter-argument and offering a compromise. Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Use negotiation language and evaluative phrasing to practise persuasive, conditional proposals.

network.learningNote: At B2 you should move from simple opinion to measured evaluation: use modal hedges (might, could), graduated adjectives (somewhat, highly), and discourse markers (however, consequently). vocabulary.definition: The tendency of customers to continue buying from the same brand over time.
vocabulary.exampleEN: High brand loyalty can reduce marketing costs because repeat customers are easier to convert. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.

vocabulary.definition: A feeling that one is accepted and part of a group or community.

vocabulary.exampleAR: أنشأ المنتدى الإلكتروني للعلامة التجارية إحساسًا قويًا بالانتماء بين العملاء الشباب. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.exampleAR: ينجح التسويق القَبَلي عندما تتوافق هوية مجموعة متخصصة عن كثب مع صورة العلامة التجارية. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: To encourage and develop customers' long-term commitment to a brand.

vocabulary.exampleAR: تساعد الفعاليات المنتظمة والمكافآت ذات المعنى على تعزيز الولاء بين العملاء. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: The quality of a message or brand that evokes an emotional response in an audience.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The campaign's emotional resonance was evident in dozens of heartfelt social posts. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ظهر التأثير العاطفي للحملة في عشرات المنشورات الاجتماعية المعبرة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: A person who promotes a brand, often enthusiastically and publicly, helping to shape its image.

vocabulary.exampleAR: يعمل المؤثرون الصغار غالبًا كسفراء علامة تجارية أصيلين للمنتجات المتخصصة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Business practices that aim to have a positive impact on society and the environment.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Corporate social responsibility initiatives can strengthen a brand's credibility with conscious consumers. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يمكن لمبادرات المسؤولية الاجتماعية للشركات أن تُقوّي مصداقية العلامة التجارية لدى المستهلكين الواعيين. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: The ability of a company to keep its customers over a specified period.
vocabulary.exampleEN: A small increase in customer retention can significantly boost long-term profits. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يمكن لزيادة صغيرة في الاحتفاظ بالعملاء أن تزيد الأرباح طويلة الأجل بشكل كبير. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: To have a strong emotional or intellectual effect on someone.

vocabulary.exampleAR: فشلت رسالتهم بشأن الاستدامة في التأثير على المتسوقين الذين يعطون الأولوية للسعر. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Actions or purchases that communicate a person's values, status, or group membership.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Buying vintage sneakers became a form of identity signalling among the group's members. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أصبح شراء الأحذية الرياضية القديمة شكلًا من أشكال إشارة الهوية بين أعضاء المجموعة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: To deliberately develop and nurture a group of engaged customers or supporters.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The brand hired a community manager to cultivate community and moderate discussions. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: استأجرت العلامة التجارية مدير مجتمع لبناء المجتمع وإدارة النقاشات. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Dividing a market into distinct groups of potential customers with similar needs or behaviours.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Careful audience segmentation helped the brand target messages that resonated with each subgroup. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ساعد تقسيم الجمهور الدقيق العلامة التجارية على توجيه رسائل تناسب كل شريحة فرعية. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

grammar.concept: Use adjectives, adverbs, evaluative verbs, modal hedges and discourse markers to qualify judgements. Use rhetorical questions to prompt the reader and highlight issues without making direct commands.
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية غالبًا تُستخدم أدوات اتصال مباشرة مثل 'ألا...' أو 'أليس من الأفضل...' مع صيغ تقريرية؛ في الإنجليزية B2 نميل إلى استخدام hedges وqualifiers لتجنب المطلقية.
grammar.structure: Key patterns: evaluative adverbs/adjectives (arguably, somewhat problematic, highly effective); hedging (might, could, appears to); evaluative verbs (undermine, bolster); rhetorical questions (Why would a customer pay for X? Isn't authenticity more important than discounts?).
grammar.commonError: Overstating claims with absolutes (always, never) or mixing informal intensifiers ('super', 'totally') with a formal evaluative register.
grammar.exampleEN: Arguably, investing in small local events is more effective at building brand loyalty than generic online ads; after all, who doesn't prefer real human connection?
grammar.exampleAR: من الجدير بالقول أن الاستثمار في فعاليات محلية صغيرة أكثر فعالية في بناء ولاء العلامة التجارية من الإعلانات الإلكترونية العامة؛ فبعد كل شيء، من لا يفضل التواصل البشري الحقيقي؟

readingBrief: Write an original feature (350–450 words) titled 'The business of belonging' that examines how modern brands create or buy loyalty. Include: (a) two short case examples—one of successful community cultivation and one where efforts appeared inauthentic; (b) a quote from a consumer and a brief comment from a marketing director; (c) analysis of tactics (events, ambassadors, CSR, digital forums) and the tension between short-term sales and long-term trust. Use evaluative language and at least two rhetorical questions. Aim for an analytical, balanced tone and conclude with a clear evaluative observation. Compare the new context with the earlier lesson and identify one shift in register or evidence.
writingPrompt: Write a 200–260 word proposal addressed to the marketing director of a mid-sized apparel brand recommending whether to invest in a community-building pilot. Purpose: evaluate two possible strategies (a series of local community events; a digital ambassador programme), recommend one, and acknowledge one main risk or counterpoint. Include: a clear recommendation, two brief reasons (use evaluative language), one mitigating action for the risk, and one rhetorical question to engage the director. Audience: marketing director (formal but persuasive). Success criteria: formal register appropriate for senior staff; cohesive organisation with clear linkers (Firstly, However, Therefore); use at least three evaluative expressions (e.g. arguably, more effective, potentially problematic); length 200–260 words. Revise the result for a different audience and explain one language choice.

network.learningNote: At B2, focus on sequencing concession and rebuttal clearly: concede briefly, then use linkers (however, on the contrary, in light of) and present specific evidence. Avoid overused single-linker openings; vary phrasing to show nuance.
network.learningNoteArabic: في مستوى B2 ركّز على ترتيب الإقرار ثم الدحض بوضوح: اعترف بإيجاز ثم استخدم وصلات (ومع ذلك، على العكس، في ضوء) وقدم أدلة محددة. تجنّب فتح الجمل بنفس الرابط دائمًا لإظهار التنوّع.

vocabulary.exampleAR: نحتاج إلى أدلة قوية قبل التوصية بتنفيذ كامل. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

grammar.concept: Use a range of discourse markers to sequence concession and rebuttal: briefly concede an opposing point, then pivot using contrastive or evaluative linkers and support your rebuttal with specific evidence or logic.
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية عادةً تُستخدم كلمات مثل 'مع أن' و'مع ذلك' و'إلا أن' بنفس وظيفة أدوات الترابط الإنجليزية، لكن البنية الإنجليزية تشجّع على جمل قِصَر متبوعة بجملة دحض مباشرة وروابط تقييمية.
grammar.structure: Concession + quick qualification, contrastive pivot + evidence/reasoning. Patterns: 'While X acknowledges Y, X fails to Z.' 'Admittedly, X; however, the data shows Y.' 'Although critics argue X, the evidence indicates Y.'
grammar.commonError: Overusing 'however' at sentence starts without varying structure; failing to follow a concession with concrete evidence (only opinion).
grammar.exampleEN: Admittedly, shorter working weeks can increase scheduling complexity; however, a recent controlled study found a 10% rise in output per hour when flexible rostering was used.
grammar.exampleAR: من المسلم به أن أسابيع العمل الأقصر قد تزيد من تعقيد الجداول؛ ومع ذلك، وجدت دراسة محكمة حديثة زيادة بنسبة 10% في الإنتاج لكل ساعة عند استخدام جداول مرنة.

readingBrief: Feature article (350–400 words): an original feature examining a year-long pilot of a four-day workweek in a midsize city. The piece summarises key findings (productivity metrics, employee wellbeing surveys, business costs), includes two short company case studies (one positive, one mixed), and reports common criticisms (service disruption, unequal impact). Learners should identify main claims, evaluate the quality of the evidence presented, and note the strongest counterargument that a sceptical stakeholder might raise. Compare the new context with the earlier lesson and identify one shift in register or evidence.
writingPrompt: Write a 200–260-word formal proposal addressed to the City Council (audience) advising whether they should expand the four-day workweek pilot (purpose). Include a concise evaluation of the evidence, acknowledge one plausible counterargument and rebut or qualify it, and finish with a clear recommendation. Success criteria: formal register, clear organisation (one-sentence intro, one paragraph evaluating evidence, one paragraph addressing the counterargument and mitigation, one-sentence conclusion), use at least two discourse markers for concession and contrast (e.g., 'Admittedly', 'however', 'in light of'), and include at least two cohesive devices to link ideas (e.g., 'therefore', 'furthermore'). Revise the result for a different audience and explain one language choice.

retrieval.purpose: إعادة استخدام مهارات B1 (وجهة نظر، دليل، نتيجة) للتحضير لمهمة أطول على مستوى B2.

retrieval.prompt: Prepare a 100-word negotiation note that summarises two stakeholders' positions (one pro, one con) and suggests a compromise measure. Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose B1 negotiation language for B2-level policy thinking.

retrieval.prompt: حضّر مذكّرة تفاوضية قصيرة (100 كلمة) تلخّص موقفَي طرفين (مؤيّد ومعارض) وتقترح تدبيرًا توفيقيًا. Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: إعادة توظيف لغة التفاوض في مستوى B1 لمهارة التفكير السياسي على مستوى B2.

priorLevelLinks: B1: expressing a viewpoint with supporting evidence
B1: writing a short review or narrative
network.learningNote: At B2, use relative clauses to add precise information (the system that was trained on historic data) and passives to emphasise actions and responsibilities (decisions were made automatically). When framing ethics, name agents where possible to avoid vagueness—passives can hide responsibility.
network.learningNoteArabic: في مستوى B2، استخدم جمل الوصل لإضافة معلومات دقيقة (النظام الذي تم تدريبه على بيانات تاريخية) والمبني للمجهول لتسليط الضوء على الإجراءات والمسؤوليات (اتخذت القرارات تلقائيًا). عند التأطير الأخلاقي، سمّ الجهات الفاعلة لتجنّب الغموض—المجهول قد يخفي المسؤولية.

wordFamilies.note: Use 'accountability' for systems and organisations; use 'be held accountable' when referring to who answers for actions.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم 'accountability' للمنظمات والأنظمة؛ واستخدم 'be held accountable' عند الإشارة إلى من يتحمل مسئولية الأفعال.

wordFamilies.note: Common collocations: mitigate risks/harm/impact.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: تراكيب شائعة: mitigate risks/harm/impact (التخفيف من المخاطر/الضرر/التأثير).

wordFamilies.note: Transparency relates to data, processes and decision criteria.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: الشفافية تتعلق بالبيانات والعمليات ومعايير اتخاذ القرار.

vocabulary.definition: A process in which software or algorithms make choices without immediate human intervention.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Automated decision-making is used to prioritise benefit applications in the pilot scheme. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يُستخدم اتخاذ القرار الآلي لتحديد أولويات طلبات المساعدات في المرحلة التجريبية. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: A systematic review of an algorithm or automated system to identify bias, errors, or harmful impacts and to recommend corrective measures.
vocabulary.exampleEN: An algorithmic audit, which was carried out by independent experts, showed that the recruitment software disadvantaged candidates from certain backgrounds. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أظهر التدقيق الخوارزمي، الذي أجرته مجموعة من الخبراء المستقلين، أن برنامج التوظيف كان يميِّز ضد المرشحين من خلفيات معينة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: To be required to explain and justify actions or decisions and accept consequences.
vocabulary.exampleEN: If the system harms users, the council must be held accountable for deployment decisions. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إذا تسبّب النظام في ضرر للمستخدمين، يجب محاسبة المجلس عن قرارات النشر. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: A legal or ethical obligation to take reasonable steps to prevent harm to others.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Public bodies have a duty of care to ensure new technologies do not discriminate. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تتحمّل الجهات العامة واجب رعاية لضمان ألا تميّز التقنيات الجديدة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Clarity about how an algorithm works, what data it uses and the criteria it applies.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Campaigners demanded algorithmic transparency so decisions could be independently reviewed. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: طالب النشطاء بشفافية الخوارزميات حتى تُراجع القرارات بشكل مستقل. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: To make something less severe, harmful, or painful.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The council introduced checks to mitigate bias before full rollout. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أدخل المجلس ضوابط لتخفيف التحيّز قبل النشر الكامل. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Results of an action that were not foreseen or intended.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Policymakers must consider unintended consequences such as exclusion or stigma. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يجب على صانعي السياسات مراعاة عواقب غير مقصودة مثل الاستبعاد أو الوصم. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Active monitoring by humans to check, correct or override automated systems.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Human oversight allows appeals when automated decisions appear unfair. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تتيح الرقابة البشرية طعونًا عندما تبدو القرارات الآلية غير عادلة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Not clear or difficult to understand; lacking transparency.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The vendor's model remained opaque, so auditors could not explain poor outcomes. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ظل نموذج المورد غامضًا، فلم يستطع المراجعون تفسير النتائج السيئة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: An evaluation that checks whether a system treats different groups equitably.
vocabulary.exampleEN: A fairness assessment found disparities in approval rates across age groups. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: وجد تقييم العدالة فروقًا في معدلات الموافقة عبر الفئات العمرية. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: A committee that reviews the moral implications of policies and technologies.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The council convened an ethics board to review the pilot and make recommendations. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: عقد المجلس مجلس أخلاقيات لمراجعة المرحلة التجريبية وتقديم توصيات. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: To put in place policies, checks or mechanisms that prevent or reduce harm.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Before expansion, the authority must implement safeguards such as manual audits. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قبل التوسيع، يجب على الجهة تنفيذ ضوابط مثل المراجعات اليدوية. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

grammar.topic: Relative clauses, passives, and ethical framing
grammar.arabicName: جمل الوصل، المبني للمجهول، والإطار الأخلاقي
grammar.concept: Use defining and non-defining relative clauses to add precision; use passive structures to highlight actions or to present facts objectively; combine these to frame ethical responsibility clearly.
grammar.arabicComparison: استخدم جمل الوصل لتعزيز الدقة (تعريفية وغير تعريفية). استخدم المبني للمجهول لتسليط الضوء على الأفعال أو تقديم الوقائع بموضوعية. اجمع بينهما لتأطير المسؤولية الأخلاقية بوضوح.
grammar.structure: Relative clause: The algorithm that was trained on historic data produced different results. Passive: Decisions were made automatically. Combined: The programme, which was endorsed last year, was deployed and decisions were made automatically.
grammar.commonError: Overuse of the passive without naming agents leads to vagueness (e.g., 'Mistakes were made' without saying who made them). Also, mixing defining and non-defining clauses incorrectly (missing commas) changes meaning.
grammar.exampleEN: The system that processed applications was updated last month. Concerns were raised, which prompted an independent review.
grammar.exampleAR: النظام الذي عالج الطلبات تم تحديثه الشهر الماضي. أُثيرت مخاوف، مما دفع لإجراء مراجعة مستقلة.

readingBrief: Write an original feature article of 350–450 words for a national newspaper that examines a recent pilot in which an automated system allocated social benefits. Include: a concise description of how the system worked; at least two pieces of evidence that point to algorithmic bias (statistics, case examples or quotes from stakeholders); comments from at least one council representative and one affected resident or campaigner; analysis of unintended consequences; and two concrete policy recommendations (for example, a fairness assessment and continued human oversight). Use relative clauses and passive structures to frame responsibility and avoid vague blame. Aim for balanced tone: evaluate benefits as well as harms, and close with a clear ethical judgement and practical next steps. Compare the new context with the earlier lesson and identify one shift in register or evidence.
writingPrompt: Write a formal letter of 200–260 words to the chair of the local council (audience: council chair and published as a letter to the editor) arguing whether the AI benefits-allocation system should be suspended pending a full audit. Purpose: evaluate the pilot evidence, acknowledge the council's concern to maintain services, and propose a qualified recommendation. Include one explicit counterpoint (e.g., disruption to service if suspended) and respond to it. Success criteria: formal register suitable for public officials; use at least two relative clauses and two passive constructions; include three vocabulary items from this lesson (e.g., algorithmic bias, human oversight, implement safeguards); present a clear recommendation and steps for accountability; organise ideas with cohesive devices for clarity. Revise the result for a different audience and explain one language choice.

title: A review that changes minds — Extension 6

outcome.canDo: I can write a concise evaluative response that weighs evidence, addresses counterpoints, and makes a carefully qualified recommendation. Apply the choice to a new B2 context.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع كتابة رد تقييمي موجز يوازن بين الأدلة، ويتناول وجهات النظر المعارضة، ويقدّم توصية مؤهّلة بدقّة. طبّق ذلك في سياق جديد من مستوى B2.
outcome.scenario: A respected cultural reviewer has published a feature suggesting major changes to a public programme. As a professional with direct responsibility, you must write a short response for the same publication that evaluates the review, highlights where its argument is strongest and weakest, and proposes a realistic next step.
outcome.scenarioArabic: نشر ناقد ثقافي مرموق مقالاً يقترح تغييرات كبيرة على برنامج عام. بصفتك محترفاً تتحمّل مسؤولية مباشرة، عليك كتابة ردّ موجز لنفس الصحيفة يقوّم المراجعة، ويُحدد أين تكون حجّتها قوية أو ضعيفة، ويقترح خطوة تالية واقعية.

retrieval.prompt: Viewpoint: Briefly restate the reviewer’s main viewpoint in one sentence. Which two words from B1 (viewpoint, evidence, consequence, negotiation, narrative, review) help you summarise it? Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Activate recall of B1 terms and focus learners on identifying the reviewer's stance.

retrieval.prompt: Evidence: List two pieces of evidence the reviewer uses. For each, note whether it is objective (facts, figures) or subjective (testimony, impression). Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Prepare learners to distinguish types of evidence for a balanced evaluation.

retrieval.prompt: Consequence: Identify one likely consequence the reviewer predicts. How might you challenge that prediction politely? Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Prompt learners to anticipate and qualify consequences in their response.

retrieval.prompt: Negotiation: Imagine you must convince a colleague who disagrees. Write a one-sentence concession (acknowledging their point) and a one-sentence rebuttal. Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Practice phrases for conceding and disagreeing—useful in nuanced evaluation.

network.learningNote: At B2 learners should use appraisal language (hedges, boosters, evaluative adjectives) to offer balanced judgments. Aim to qualify claims rather than make absolute statements. Use discourse markers (however, nevertheless, on balance) to structure nuanced responses.
network.learningNoteArabic: يجب على متعلمي المستوى B2 استخدام لغة التقييم (التلطيف، التعزيز، الصفات التقييمية) لتقديم أحكام متوازنة. هدفك هو تقييد الادعاءات بدلاً من إطلاق أحكام مطلقة. استخدم روابط الخطاب (مع ذلك، ومع ذلك، في المجمل) لتنظيم الردود الدقيقة.

wordFamilies.note: Use recommend + (that) + clause for formal suggestions, or recommend + noun for proposals.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم recommend + (that) + جملة للاقتراحات الرسمية، أو recommend + اسم للتوصيات.

wordFamilies.note: Critical can be neutral (important) or negative—context and hedging show the tone.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: قد تكون critical محايدة (ذات أهمية) أو سلبية — السياق والتلطيف يوضّحان النغمة.

wordFamilies.note: Evaluation focuses on criteria; make these explicit (e.g. impact, cost, fairness).
wordFamilies.noteArabic: التقييم يركّز على المعايير؛ اجعلها واضحة (مثل الأثر، التكلفة، العدالة).

vocabulary.arabic: بعد أخذ كل الأمور بعين الاعتبار
vocabulary.definition: used to introduce a measured conclusion after weighing various positive and negative factors
vocabulary.exampleEN: All things considered, the book's insightful analysis compensates for its dense style. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعد أخذ كل الأمور بعين الاعتبار، يعوّض التحليل العميق في الكتاب عن أسلوبه الكثيف. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: expressing agreement or approval but noting concerns
vocabulary.exampleEN: I accept the proposal with reservations about the budget estimates. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أوافق على الاقتراح مع تحفظات بشأن تقديرات الميزانية. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: supported by reliable data or research
vocabulary.exampleEN: The committee must make an evidence-based decision rather than rely on anecdotes. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يجب على اللجنة اتخاذ قرار مبني على الأدلة بدلاً من الاعتماد على الروايات. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: indicates that something causes significant worry
vocabulary.exampleEN: The omission of safety checks raises serious concerns about the programme’s rollout. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إهمال فحوصات السلامة يثير مخاوف جدية بشأن إطلاق البرنامج. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: presents strong reasons that are likely to persuade
vocabulary.exampleEN: The feature offers a compelling case for redesigning the visitor route. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يقدّم التقرير حجة مقنعة لإعادة تصميم مسار الزوار. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: difficult to provide a valid reason for
vocabulary.exampleEN: Cutting community workshops at this stage is hard to justify. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يُعدّ خفض ورش العمل المجتمعية في هذه المرحلة أمراً يصعب تبريره. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: thorough, careful, and exact
vocabulary.exampleEN: We need a more rigorous evaluation of the pilot before scaling up. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: نحتاج إلى تقييم أكثر دقة للتجربة قبل التوسّع. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: unclear or open to more than one interpretation
vocabulary.exampleEN: Some of the reviewer’s claims are ambiguous and need clarification. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعض مزاعم الناقد غامضة وتحتاج إلى توضيح. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: showing subtle differences in meaning or judgement
vocabulary.exampleEN: A nuanced response acknowledges strengths while flagging risks. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ردّ ذو فوارق دقيقة يعترف بالنقاط القوية ويشير إلى المخاطر. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: to state doubts or concerns about something
vocabulary.exampleEN: Several stakeholders expressed reservations about the timeline. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أعرب العديد من أصحاب المصلحة عن تحفظاتهم بشأن الجدول الزمني. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: to give a suggestion while signalling limits or conditions
vocabulary.exampleEN: I would recommend cautiously introducing the change in one region first. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أوصي بحذر بإدخال التغيير في منطقة واحدة أولاً. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: to limit or modify a statement to make it less absolute
vocabulary.exampleEN: She qualified her praise with a note about long-term costs. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قيدت مدحها بملاحظة عن التكاليف على المدى الطويل. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

grammar.concept: Use hedging, boosters and evaluative vocabulary to make balanced judgments; explicitly state criteria and acknowledge counterarguments.
grammar.arabicComparison: استخدم التلطيف والتقوية والمفردات التقييمية لتقديم أحكام متوازنة؛ اذكر المعايير واعترف بالحجج المعارضة.
grammar.structure: Common structures: 'It would be more accurate to say that...', 'While X acknowledges Y, it overlooks Z', 'On balance, I would recommend X, provided that Y is addressed.' Use modal verbs (might, could), adverbs (arguably, perhaps), and contrast markers (however, nevertheless).
grammar.commonError: Making absolute claims (e.g. 'This is wrong') without qualification, or failing to link claims to explicit evidence and criteria.
grammar.exampleEN: While the report offers a compelling case for expansion, it is arguably premature without a rigorous cost–benefit analysis.
grammar.exampleAR: بينما يقدّم التقرير حجة مقنعة للتوسّع، فمن الجدير بالقول أنه سابق لأوانه دون تحليل دقيق للتكاليف والعوائد.

readingBrief: Write an original 350–450-word feature article for a national newspaper that examines a single critical review whose publication changed public opinion and led local decision-makers to reconsider a major cultural programme. The article should summarise the reviewer’s main arguments, assess the quality and types of evidence used (e.g. statistics, expert testimony, visitor feedback), quote at least two short reactions (one from a supporter, one from a critic), and analyse why the review succeeded in persuading readers and officials. Conclude with a concise statement of what criteria should guide any follow-up decisions (e.g. impact, cost, equity). Tone: balanced and analytical; audience: informed general readers. Compare the new context with the earlier lesson and identify one shift in register or evidence.
writingPrompt: Write a 200–260-word letter to the editor of the same newspaper. Your purpose is to evaluate the review and to propose a single, realistic next step for the programme. Address a professional audience (editors, local council members). You must: 1) acknowledge at least one valid counterpoint from the original review; 2) use at least two appraisal expressions from the lesson vocabulary (e.g. 'on balance', 'with reservations', 'evidence-based'); 3) keep a formal but measured register and include clear linking devices (however, nevertheless, therefore, for example). Success criteria: formal register, three short paragraphs (opening evaluation, counterpoint and rebuttal, clear recommendation with qualification), and cohesion through explicit linking phrases. Revise the result for a different audience and explain one language choice.

title: Learning from disagreement — Extension 6

outcome.canDo: I can reformulate another person's view and make a respectful challenge that includes evidence and a concrete proposal. Apply the choice to a new B2 context.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع إعادة صياغة رأي الآخر وتقديم تحدٍ محترم يتضمن دليلاً واقتراحًا ملموسًا. طبّق ذلك في سياق جديد من مستوى B2.
outcome.scenario: After reading a local feature about proposals to convert a neighbourhood garden into a café, you will write a response to the editor that evaluates the main arguments, acknowledges valid concerns, raises one well‑reasoned objection, and proposes a compromise solution.
outcome.scenarioArabic: بعد قراءة مقال محلي حول اقتراح تحويل حديقة الحي إلى مقهى، ستكتب ردًا إلى المحرر يقيّم فيه الحجج الرئيسية، يعترف بالمخاوف المشروعة، يقدّم اعتراضًا مدعومًا جيدًا، ويقترح حلًّا وسطيًا.

retrieval.prompt: Read this short comment (60–80 words). Identify the writer's viewpoint, then quickly reframe it in one sentence and state one piece of evidence they use. (Focus word: viewpoint) Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Practice turning a B1 concept (viewpoint) into a precise B2 reformulation.

retrieval.prompt: اقرأ الفقرة القصيرة. حدد ما هو الدليل الذي يستخدمه الكاتب ثم اعرض الآن رداً موجزاً يعيد صياغة وجهة نظره ويطرح سؤالاً استيضاحيًا. (الكلمة المحورية: evidence) Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: استخدام مصطلح مستوى B1 (evidence) داخل مهمة كتابة مستوى B2.

retrieval.prompt: Given a short paragraph describing likely outcomes, state the main consequence the author predicts, then propose one mitigation. (Focus word: consequence) Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Train B2 learners to evaluate consequences and suggest responses.

retrieval.prompt: اقرأ سردًا قصيرًا عن مفاوضات محلية. لخص موقف أحد الأطراف ثم اكتب اقتراحًا واحدًا للتفاوض بنبرة محترمة. (الكلمة المحورية: negotiation) Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: تحويل مهارة التفاوض (B1) إلى كتابة واقتراحات بنبرة محترمة (B2).

network.learningNote: At B2 we focus on reformulating others' ideas accurately and challenging them respectfully: use hedging (e.g. 'I wonder whether…'), signal agreement before disagreement, and always supply evidence or a concrete alternative.
network.learningNoteArabic: في مستوى B2 نركّز على إعادة صياغة أفكار الآخرين بدقة وتحدّيها باحترام: استخدم عبارات التخفيف (مثل «أتساءل هل…»)، وأشر إلى موافقة جزئية قبل الاختلاف، وادعم رأيك بدليل أو بديل عملي.

wordFamilies.note: Use to admit a point while keeping your main argument; useful in polite disagreement.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: للاعتراف بنقطة بينما تحافظ على حجتك الرئيسية؛ مفيد في الخلاف المهذب.

wordFamilies.note: Can be neutral (to test an idea) or confrontational; pair with 'respectful' for polite language.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: قد تكون محايدة (لاختبار فكرة) أو تصادمية؛ اقترن بكلمة «محترم» للفظ مهذب.

wordFamilies.note: Useful to offer alternatives or compromise during disagreement.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: مفيد لتقديم بدائل أو حلول وسط أثناء الخلاف.

vocabulary.definition: Express someone else's idea in different words that highlight a particular aspect or implication.
vocabulary.exampleEN: To reframe her point, you might stress how the proposal benefits young families rather than its cost. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: لإعادة صياغة وجهة نظرها، يمكنك التأكيد على كيف يفيد الاقتراح العائلات الشابة بدلًا من التركيز على التكلفة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: A disagreement expressed politely, usually acknowledging something valid before raising an objection.
vocabulary.exampleEN: He offered a respectful challenge by first praising the idea, then questioning its feasibility. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قدّم تحديًا محترمًا بمدح الفكرة أولًا ثم التساؤل عن قابليتها للتنفيذ. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Deliberately argue the opposite position to test the strength of an idea.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I'll play devil's advocate for a moment: what if the café brought too many visitors? Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سألعب دور محامي الشيطان للحظة: ماذا لو جلب المقهى عددًا كبيرًا من الزوار؟ استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: To state disagreement or disapproval, especially in a discussion or decision-making context.
vocabulary.exampleEN: When the committee proposed extending opening hours, two senior staff voiced dissent, suggesting it would strain current rotas. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: عندما اقترحت اللجنةُ تمديدَ ساعاتِ العمل، أعربَ اثنانُ من كبار الموظفين عن معارضتهما، مؤكدين أنه سيجهدُ جداولَ العمل الحالية. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Considering all aspects, perspectives, or consequences of a matter rather than focusing on a single element.
vocabulary.exampleEN: In the round, the policy has benefits and drawbacks, so we should reformulate it to address the main concerns. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: من جميعِ الجوانب، لدى السياسةِ فوائدٌ ومساوئٌ، لذا ينبغي علينا إعادةَ صياغتها لمعالجةِ المخاوفِ الرئيسية. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Shared interests or opinions that parties in a disagreement can agree on.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Finding common ground helped them reach a quicker compromise. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: ساعد إيجاد القواسم المشتركة على الوصول إلى حل وسط أسرع. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Say that part of someone else's argument is valid before presenting your own point.
vocabulary.exampleEN: She took time to acknowledge the value of the volunteers' work before suggesting changes. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أعطت وقتًا للاعتراف بقيمة عمل المتطوعين قبل اقتراح التغييرات. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Suggest an alternative plan intended to replace or improve the original proposal.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Rather than rejecting the plan, they offered a counterproposal with reduced opening hours. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بدلًا من رفض الخطة، قدموا اقتراحًا مضادًا بساعات عمل مخففة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: A subtle distinction or slight variation in meaning, feeling, or tone.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Her argument has important nuances that deserve attention. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: لحجتها فروق دقيقة مهمة تستحق الانتباه. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: A particular attitude or way of regarding something; a point of view.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Try to understand the residents' perspective before judging the proposal. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: حاول أن تفهم وجهة نظر السكان قبل الحكم على الاقتراح. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Admit that something is true or valid, often reluctantly.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I concede that parking is a legitimate concern for nearby residents. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أعترف أن موقف السيارات يمثل قلقًا مشروعًا للسكان القريبين. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Provide evidence to support or prove a claim.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Can the council substantiate its claim that the café will create local jobs? Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: هل يمكن للمجلس أن يثبت بدليل زعمه أن المقهى سيخلق وظائف محلية؟ استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

grammar.concept: Techniques and language to restate another speaker's point clearly (reformulation) and to disagree politely while supplying reasons or alternatives (respectful challenge).
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية نستخدم أحيانًا صيغة مثل «أفهم أنك تقول… لكن…» أو «لدي تحفظ بسيط»، وهذه مكافِئة لإعادة الصياغة ثم التحدي المحترم في الإنجليزية.
grammar.structure: Useful frames: 'If I understand you correctly, you're saying that…' / 'I see your point, however…' / 'I agree to an extent, but…' / 'I acknowledge that…, yet I would suggest…' / 'Have you considered…?' / 'One concern is…; perhaps we could…'.
grammar.commonError: Learners often switch directly to disagreement without acknowledging the other side, which sounds confrontational. Also, overuse of absolutes ('never', 'always') weakens polite challenge.
grammar.exampleEN: 'If I understand you correctly, you're worried about noise from the café. I see your point, however, a limited timetable could reduce late‑night noise while still supporting local business.'
grammar.exampleAR: «إذا فهمت قصدك، فأنت قلق من الضوضاء الناتجة عن المقهى. أرى وجهة نظرك، ومع ذلك يمكن لجدول زمني محدود أن يقلل الضجيج الليلي ويدعم الأعمال المحلية في الوقت نفسه.»

readingBrief: Write an original 350–450-word feature article for a local community newsletter. The piece should report on a recent council proposal to convert a small neighbourhood garden into a café. Include: quotes from at least two residents with opposing views, one short comment from a council representative, clear description of likely consequences (positive and negative), and a brief account of attempts to negotiate (e.g. meetings or consultations). The tone should be balanced — present evidence, highlight nuances, and end by suggesting one practical compromise that could address the main concerns. Compare the new context with the earlier lesson and identify one shift in register or evidence.
writingPrompt: Write a 200–260-word letter to the editor of the community newsletter in response to the feature described above. Audience: local readers and council members. Purpose: evaluate the main arguments, acknowledge a valid counterpoint, raise one respectful objection with supporting reasoning, and propose a feasible compromise. Include one reformulation of another person's point (use a frame such as 'If I understand you correctly...') and one respectful challenge (use a frame such as 'I see your point, however...'). Success criteria: formal-but-approachable register appropriate for local debate, explicit cohesive linking (contrast, concession, cause/effect), clear final proposal, and adherence to the 200–260 word count. Revise the result for a different audience and explain one language choice.

title: A proposal with consequences — Extension 6

outcome.canDo: I can evaluate a public policy proposal, recommend a modified plan and predict likely outcomes using formal language, hedging and evidence. Apply the choice to a new B2 context.

retrieval.prompt: Viewpoint — Write a single formal opening sentence that states your position on the proposal (support, oppose or amend). Use language appropriate for a council report. Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Repurposes the B1 skill of giving a viewpoint into a concise formal stance suitable for B2 argumentative writing.

retrieval.purpose: Transforms the B1 idea of 'evidence' into selecting and using appropriate evidence for policy arguments at B2 level.

retrieval.prompt: Consequence — Draft one paragraph (40–60 words) projecting two likely outcomes of the original proposal and one unintended consequence, using hedging language (may, might, be likely to). Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.

retrieval.prompt: Negotiation — Prepare two short sentences that respond to an opposing stakeholder: acknowledge their point and offer a compromise (use formal negotiation phrases). Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.

network.learningNote: Focus on formal recommendation language (recommend, advise, propose) and careful hedging (may, might, be likely to). Teach multi-word discourse chunks used in policy writing and how to balance clear stance with cautious projection.
network.learningNoteArabic: ركز على لغة التوصيات الرسمية (recommend, advise, propose) والتلطيف باستخدام may/might وbe likely to. علم عبارات متعددة الكلمات المستخدمة فى كتابة السياسات وكيفية الموازنة بين موقف واضح وتنبؤ محاط بالحذر.

wordFamilies.note: Use the noun 'implementation' for the phase when a policy is put into practice.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم الاسم 'implementation' للمرحلة التى تُطبّق فيها السياسة.

wordFamilies.note: As verb and noun; 'projection' and 'projected' are useful for forecasting outcomes.

vocabulary.definition: To formally present an idea or plan for consideration.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The committee put forward a proposal to pedestrianise the town centre on weekends. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: طرحت اللجنة مقترحًا لتحويل مركز المدينة إلى منطقة للمشاة نهاية كل أسبوع. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: To perform a systematic evaluation of a plan or situation.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Before approving the scheme, they will carry out an environmental assessment. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قبل الموافقة على الخطة، سيجرون تقييمًا بيئيًا. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: The stage in a project when planned actions are put into practice.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Delays during the implementation phase can increase costs considerably. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يمكن أن تؤدى التأخيرات خلال مرحلة التنفيذ إلى زيادة التكاليف بشكل كبير. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: A detailed plan that sets out phases, timelines, responsibilities and milestones for carrying out a policy or project.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The committee produced an implementation roadmap so that each phase of the education reform had clear milestones and accountable teams. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أعدت اللجنة خارطة طريق للتنفيذ بحيث تكون لكل مرحلة من إصلاح التعليم معالم زمنية واضحة وفرق مسؤولة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: An estimate of the likely effects of a policy or action.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The projected impact includes a 15% reduction in traffic within two years. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يشمل الأثر المتوقع انخفاضًا فى حركة المرور بنسبة 15% خلال عامين. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Actions designed to reduce negative effects or risks.
vocabulary.exampleEN: They proposed mitigating measures such as improved public transport and exemptions for deliveries. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: اقترحوا تدابير تخفيفية مثل تحسين النقل العام وإعفاءات لعمليات التوصيل. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: The organisation or body charged with putting a policy, programme or project into practice, coordinating resources and reporting progress.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The council appointed a single implementing agency to oversee the pilot scheme and to report projected outcomes to stakeholders. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: عين المجلس جهة منفذة واحدة للإشراف على المشروع التجريبي وتقديم تقارير عن النتائج المتوقعة لأصحاب المصلحة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Possible and practical to do easily or within the resources available.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The plan is only feasible if the council secures additional funding. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الخطة ممكنة فقط إذا حصل المجلس على تمويل إضافى. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: A backup plan designed for unexpected events.
vocabulary.exampleEN: A contingency should be included in the budget for sudden cost increases. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يجب تضمين خطة طوارئ فى الميزانية لمواجهة الزيادات المفاجئة فى التكاليف. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: To weaken or damage something gradually.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Poor communication will undermine public trust in the scheme. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سوف يقلل الاتصال الضعيف من ثقة الجمهور فى الخطة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: The process of asking for opinions from people affected by a decision.
vocabulary.exampleEN: The council launched a consultation to collect residents' views on the proposal. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أطلق المجلس مشاورة لجمع آراء السكان حول المقترح. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Numerical information used to measure and compare outcomes.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Quantitative data from the pilot showed a clear drop in vehicle numbers. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: أظهرت البيانات الكمية من المشروع التجريبى انخفاضًا واضحًا فى أعداد المركبات. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

grammar.concept: Use formal recommendation structures (recommend that, should, ought to, propose) together with hedging and modal verbs (may, might, could) to present cautious forecasts. Combine these with future-oriented expressions (will, be likely to, projection) and conditional sentences to predict outcomes and show contingency.
grammar.arabicComparison: فى العربية تُستخدم صيغ مثل يجب/ينبغي للتوصية والعبارات الاحتمالية مثل من المحتمل/قد للتلطيف. الإنجليزية فى المستوى الرسمى تميّز بين 'should' للتوصية و'may/might' للتوقع غير المؤكد.
grammar.structure: Recommendation: I recommend that + subject + (should) + base verb. / Formal proposal: We propose that + subject + (be) + past participle (for passive). / Hedging: This may/might/could result in + noun / Projection: Subject + is likely to + verb / Conditional projection: If + present simple, + will + base verb.
grammar.commonError: Confusing 'should' (suggestion) with 'must' (obligation) and overusing 'will' when uncertain — use 'may/might' instead to hedge forecasts.
grammar.exampleEN: I recommend that the council carry out an independent assessment. If the pilot is successful, the measure is likely to reduce traffic by up to 15%, but it may cause short-term disruption.
grammar.exampleAR: أوصى بأن يجري المجلس تقييمًا مستقلًا. إذا نجح المشروع التجريبى، فمن المرجح أن يقلل الإجراء حركة المرور بما يصل إلى 15%، لكنه قد يسبب اضطرابًا مؤقتًا.

readingBrief: You will read an original feature (350–450 words): an interview with a city planner about a proposed 'low-traffic neighbourhood' scheme. The article explains the planner's recommended version of the proposal, summarises quantitative data from a recent pilot, and discusses likely benefits (improved air quality, safer streets) alongside unintended consequences (diverted traffic to neighbouring roads, impact on local deliveries). It includes quotes from residents and traders, a short summary of a cost–benefit analysis, and suggested mitigating measures and an implementation timeline. Focus tasks: identify the writer's recommendations, evaluate the quality of evidence, recognise hedging language and projected outcomes, and note where stakeholders' concerns are acknowledged. Compare the new context with the earlier lesson and identify one shift in register or evidence.
writingPrompt: Write a formal memorandum of 200–260 words to the City Council (audience: councillors and senior officers). Purpose: propose a modified version of the traffic-management plan that balances environmental and business concerns. Include: a clear recommendation, two supporting points of evidence (one qualitative, one quantitative), one acknowledged counterargument with a mitigating measure, and a realistic projected outcome with hedging language. Success criteria: 200–260 words; formal register throughout; include at least two hedging expressions (may, might, be likely to); use three linking phrases (e.g., however, therefore, as a result) to ensure cohesion; and include one implementation step with a brief timescale. Revise the result for a different audience and explain one language choice.

title: Work, purpose, and pressure — Extension 6

outcome.canDo: Argue for or against company measures to reduce burnout, evaluate evidence and trade-offs, and propose a practical plan using varied verb patterns and emphasis for clarity. Apply the choice to a new B2 context.
outcome.canDoArabic: القدرة على الدفاع عن أو معارضة تدابير الشركة لتقليل الإرهاق، وتقييم الأدلة والمقايضات، واقتراح خطة عملية باستخدام أنماط أفعال متنوعة وأساليب للتشديد من أجل الوضوح. طبّق ذلك في سياق جديد من مستوى B2.
outcome.scenario: You have received a message from a colleague expressing concern that the company lacks meaningful work and that pressure is causing burnout. outcome.scenarioArabic: تلقيت رسالة من زميل يعبر عن قلقه من أن الشركة تفتقر إلى عمل ذي معنى وأن الضغوط تتسبب في الإرهاق. اكتب ردًا متأنيًا للزميل ومقترحًا موجزًا لإدارة الموارد البشرية يقيّم المشكلات، ويوازن الأدلة، ويوصي بخطوتين واقعيتين.

retrieval.prompt: Viewpoint — From the reading, identify two opposing viewpoints about whether meaningful work or workload is the main cause of burnout. Decide which viewpoint you support and explain why, considering weaknesses in both. Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Practice forming balanced, evidence-based evaluations of viewpoints (B1 viewpoint → B2 critical evaluation).

retrieval.prompt: Evidence — List three pieces of evidence the article uses (e.g. statistic, interview quote, policy example). For each, judge how convincing it is and say what further evidence would strengthen it. Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Move from recognising evidence to judging its reliability and gaps.

retrieval.prompt: Consequence — Predict two possible consequences of introducing a four-day week vs. hiring extra staff. Support each prediction with reasoning and acknowledge one uncertainty. Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Develop causal reasoning and qualified forecasting (B1 consequence → B2 nuanced prediction).

retrieval.prompt: Negotiation — Draft a short message (60–80 words) proposing a phased solution to HR that balances budget limits and staff wellbeing; offer one concession you would accept. Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Move from simple negotiation language to making realistic compromises and proposals.

wordFamilies.note: Used both as literal motion and metaphorically (be driven by = motivated by).

wordFamilies.noteArabic: مفيدة عند مناقشة الرضا الوظيفي وما يجعل العمل مُجزياً.

wordFamilies.note: Use to talk about work-life balance and correcting imbalances.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: تُستخدم للحديث عن توازن العمل والحياة وتصحيح الاختلالات.

vocabulary.definition: A feeling that one's work has meaning and contributes to something important.

vocabulary.exampleAR: بقيت في المنصب لأنها كانت تُشعر بإحساس قوي بالهدف. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: A state of physical and emotional exhaustion caused by prolonged stress at work.
vocabulary.exampleEN: After months of unpaid overtime he experienced severe burnout. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعد أشهر من العمل الإضافي دون أجر عانى من إرهاق مهني شديد. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Work that is perceived as worthwhile, valuable or aligned with personal values.
vocabulary.exampleEN: Volunteering gave her more meaningful work than her previous job. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.

vocabulary.definition: The effort required to manage feelings and display appropriate emotions at work.

vocabulary.definition: The extent to which people like or are content with their job.

vocabulary.definition: To decide that something is more important than other things and act accordingly.

vocabulary.definition: To understand and share the feelings of another person.

grammar.concept: Distinguish verb + to-infinitive vs verb + -ing, verbs that take object + to-infinitive (ask somebody to do), and use structures for emphasis (clefts, fronting, 'do' support, inversion after negatives).
grammar.arabicComparison: تمييز بين الفعل + to-infinitive و الفعل + -ing، والأفعال التي تتبعها مفعول + to-infinitive، واستخدام تراكيب للتشديد (جمل cleft، التقديم، do للتأكيد، والعكس بعد أدوات النفي).
grammar.structure: Examples: 'I want you to take a break.' (verb + object + to-infinitive); 'She enjoys teaching.' (verb + -ing); emphasis: 'It was flexible hours that improved morale.' (cleft); 'Never have I seen such exhaustion.' (inversion).
grammar.commonError: Confusing gerund and infinitive (e.g. say 'I suggest to take a break' instead of 'I suggest taking a break') and overusing informal patterns in formal proposals.
grammar.exampleEN: Correct: 'I recommend hiring extra staff to reduce workload.' / Emphasis: 'It is recognition, not pay, that many staff value most.'
grammar.exampleAR: صحيح: 'أوصي بتوظيف موظفين إضافيين لتقليل عبء العمل.' / للتشديد: 'إنما التقدير، لا الأجر، ما يقدره الكثير من الموظفين أكثر.'

readingBrief: Write an original feature (350–450 words) titled 'Why meaningful work matters — and what employers can do'. Target readers: HR professionals and managers. Include: a concise overview of the problem (linking meaningful work to burnout), one statistic (plausible and cited in-text), two short interview quotes (from an employee and an HR director) that show contrasting experiences, an evaluation of two common employer responses (e.g. flexible hours, training) plus their pros and cons, and two practical, evidence-based recommendations for organisations. Use a balanced, slightly formal tone and include at least one example of emphasis (e.g. a cleft sentence or fronted phrase). Compare the new context with the earlier lesson and identify one shift in register or evidence.
writingPrompt: Write 200–260 words addressed to the HR Director (begin 'Dear Ms Khan,') responding to the colleague's complaint about lack of purpose and pressure. Purpose: briefly evaluate the colleague's points, propose two realistic actions the company could take, and acknowledge one likely constraint (e.g. budget or timeline). Include a clear recommendation that is qualified (e.g. 'I suggest... provided that...') and a short closing sentence offering to discuss further. Success criteria: formal but conversational register, use at least two target multi-word chunks from the lesson (e.g. 'sense of purpose', 'work-life balance'), use at least one complex verb pattern (verb + object + to-infinitive or verb + -ing contrast), and organise ideas into 3–4 coherent paragraphs with linking language and one emphatic structure for clarity. Revise the result for a different audience and explain one language choice.

grammar.concept: Use conditionals and evaluative language to present balanced arguments: explain possible outcomes, show cause and effect, and qualify recommendations. Combine first and second conditionals with discourse markers to weigh options.
grammar.arabicComparison: قارن بين نتائج بديلة باستخدام شروط منطقية (إذا... فـ) وأداة تأكيد أو تليين للحكم.
grammar.structure: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base (If we preserve the market, we will retain tourism income). Second conditional for hypothetical evaluation: If + past simple, would + base (If we preserved it, we would attract visitors). Formal connectors: provided that / unless / in the event of / otherwise.
grammar.commonError: Students often put 'will' in the if-clause (incorrect: If we will preserve…). They also mix tenses across clauses, which weakens the consequence.
grammar.exampleEN: If the council allows partial redevelopment, it will create jobs while preserving the market's character.
grammar.exampleAR: إذا سمح المجلس بإعادة تطوير جزئية، فسيخلق ذلك وظائف مع الحفاظ على طابع السوق.

readingBrief: Read a 350–450-word feature article about a real city debate: the council proposes replacing a historic market with a new transport hub. The feature includes: quotes from a conservationist, a developer and two local residents; a summary of an environmental impact assessment; data on projected passenger numbers and job creation; and balanced commentary by the feature writer. Look for: stated viewpoints, evidence used, conditional statements describing likely consequences, and any proposed compromises. Your task after reading: identify the main arguments for and against, extract two pieces of strong evidence for each side, note any conditional consequences the author presents, and prepare to write a 200–260-word proposal responding to the issue. Compare the new context with the earlier lesson and identify one shift in register or evidence.
writingPrompt: Write a 200–260-word proposal for the local council and the community newsletter. Audience: local councillors and community readers. Purpose: evaluate the council's demolition plan and propose a justified compromise that preserves key heritage features while allowing necessary development. Include: an acknowledgement of the council's economic case, at least one clear conditional sentence showing consequences, and one practical proposal (e.g. adaptive reuse, partial redevelopment, or relocation). Success criteria: formal but approachable register, balanced tone (acknowledge the counterargument), use at least two vocabulary chunks from the lesson (e.g. 'heritage site', 'environmental impact assessment', 'to strike a balance', 'adaptive reuse'), and clear cohesion (use connectors such as however, therefore, provided that). grammar.topic: Integrated B2 argument, register, and cohesion
grammar.concept: Combine clear claims, hedging, concession, evidence, and a concise recommendation. Use formal discourse markers and cohesive devices to guide the reader through evaluation and proposal.
grammar.arabicComparison: قارن هذا مع B1 حيث تكون العبارات أبسط؛ في B2 تحتاج إلى تحفّظ (hedging)، تنازل (concession)، وأدلة محددة لت ترسيخ الرأي.
grammar.structure: Claim + Brief concession + Weighing of evidence + Recommendation/proposal. Use linking phrases: nevertheless, despite this, on balance, consequently, therefore.
grammar.commonError: Overloading the letter with facts without a clear stance, or mixing informal language with formal recommendations (e.g., slang + 'therefore').
grammar.exampleEN: Claim: I support keeping the library open. Concession: I accept the financial pressure on the council; however, evidence from usage figures suggests the library contributes to local employment and education. Recommendation: On balance, I propose a short-term community partnership to cover costs while exploring alternative revenue streams.
grammar.exampleAR: القول: أنا أؤيد إبقاء المكتبة مفتوحة. التنازل: أقرّ بضغوط الميزانية على المجلس؛ ومع ذلك، تشير أرقام الاستخدام إلى أن المكتبة تسهم في التوظيف والتعليم المحلي. التوصية: في المجمل، أقترح شراكة مجتمعية قصيرة الأجل لتغطية التكاليف مع البحث عن مصادر دخل بديلة.

readingBrief: Original feature (350–450 words): A 380-word local-feature exploring the council's proposal to sell the central public library to cover a budget shortfall. The piece includes a short interview with the library manager, a councillor explaining the financial argument, a parent who uses the library for children's activities, and a nearby town's example where a library was repurposed successfully. It gives three key facts (annual visitor numbers, programme attendance, estimated sale value) and quotes expressing both practical financial concerns and the intangible value of communal space. Tone: balanced but slightly sceptical about a quick sale. Compare the new context with the earlier lesson and identify one shift in register or evidence.
writingPrompt: Write a 200–260 word letter to the editor of the local newspaper in response to the original piece. Audience: local newspaper readers and council members. Purpose: defend the library’s importance, acknowledge the council’s budgetary concerns, and propose a practical compromise or alternative. You must: (1) state your position clearly in the first paragraph, (2) concede one valid point from the opposing view, (3) use at least two pieces of evidence from the reading brief (mention them), (4) propose a two-point compromise or alternative, and (5) use formal but accessible register with cohesive devices (use at least one concession phrase such as 'while I accept', 'although', or 'despite'). Success criteria: formal/mixed register appropriate for public readership, clear logical flow with cohesive linking phrases (at least four: e.g., nevertheless, on balance, consequently, therefore), one explicit concession, and a precise recommendation. Aim for a balanced, reasoned tone rather than emotive language. Revise the result for a different audience and explain one language choice.

title: Information under pressure — Extension 7

network.learningNote: At B2 we focus on fine-tuning how you represent others' words (reporting verbs) and how confident you sound (hedging and modal verbs). Choose verbs and adverbs to show exactly how strongly you stand behind a claim.

vocabulary.definition: A statement asserting that something is true, often needing proof.

vocabulary.definition: To indicate reasons to be sceptical about a claim or source.

vocabulary.exampleAR: البيانات الجديدة تثير الشكوك حول الإحصائية الأصلية. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Original material or direct evidence (e.g., official report, interview, dataset).

vocabulary.exampleAR: الإحصائية شُكك فيها بعد أن وجد المحللون خطأً. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: A claim supported by reliable evidence or verification.

vocabulary.exampleAR: يجب عرض الادعاءات المثبتة بالأدلة فقط كحقائق في التقرير. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.word: take with a grain of salt
vocabulary.definition: To be sceptical about the accuracy or truth of something.
vocabulary.exampleEN: I would take that online post with a grain of salt until we see the data. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: سأتعامل مع ذلك المنشور على الإنترنت بشيء من الحذر حتى نرى البيانات. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: To weaken the credibility or strength of a claim.

vocabulary.exampleAR: البيانات المتضاربة للشهود قد تقوّض الادعاء. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: Used to give a considered overall judgement after weighing evidence.

vocabulary.exampleAR: بعد الموازنة، الأدلة لا تربط بشكل قاطع السياسة بالزيادة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

grammar.topic: Reporting verbs and degrees of certainty
grammar.concept: Choose reporting verbs (claim, assert, suggest, admit, deny) and hedging language (may, might, appears, seems) to reflect how strongly you accept a proposition. Combine with source attribution to show responsibility.
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية يُستخدم غالبًا «قال إن» أو «أفاد أن» دون اختلافات دقيقة بين درجات التأكد؛ في الإنجليزية نستخدم أفعالًا مختلفة وعبارات تلطيفية لتبيان مدى ثقتنا بالادعاء.
grammar.structure: Subject + reporting verb (+ that-clause / + to-infinitive / + direct quote). Add modal verbs or adverbs for certainty: e.g. 'Researchers claim that X', 'The study suggests that X', 'Officials admit that X may be linked to Y'.
grammar.commonError: Mixing a strong reporting verb with a weak hedge (e.g., 'He insists that may...') or failing to adjust verb tense in reported speech.
grammar.exampleEN: The minister acknowledged that the figures may be incomplete, but insisted the overall trend was clear.
grammar.exampleAR: اعترف الوزير بأن الأرقام قد تكون غير كاملة، لكنه أصرّ على أن الاتجاه العام واضح.

readingBrief: Read an original feature (350–450 words) investigating a widely shared online claim that the new local health policy caused a 20% rise in hospital visits. The feature includes: an extract from a leaked internal memo, quotes from a peer-reviewed study, short interviews with a public-health researcher and a hospital administrator, and a social-media snapshot showing public reaction. As you read, note the types of sources used, any inconsistencies between them, and where the author uses hedging or strong reporting verbs. Compare the new context with the earlier lesson and identify one shift in register or evidence.
writingPrompt: Write a 200–260-word letter to the editor of the community fact-checking page. Purpose: argue whether the editor should publish an immediate correction, publish a cautiously worded follow-up, or delay until further verification. Include: (1) an assessment of the most and least reliable sources from the feature, (2) two concrete verification steps you propose, and (3) a short qualified recommendation (e.g., 'on balance, I recommend... but with reservation because...'). Audience: the editor and an informed public readership. Success criteria: formal but accessible register, use of at least two reporting verbs and two hedges/modals to show degrees of certainty, explicit reference to at least two source types from the article, and clear cohesive linking between points. Revise the result for a different audience and explain one language choice.

title: The price of convenience — Extension 7

outcome.canDo: I can evaluate the costs and benefits of convenient services, qualify my claims with concession language, and write a balanced 200–260-word proposal that acknowledges trade-offs and suggests practical alternatives. Apply the choice to a new B2 context.

retrieval.prompt: Viewpoint (B1 → B2): Write a 80–100-word viewpoint that summarises a customer's praise for convenience, then add one sentence of concession (start with 'Although') that recognises a valid counterpoint. Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.

retrieval.prompt: Negotiation: Draft a 60–80-word negotiation response a shopper could send to a delivery company asking for greener options; include a softening phrase (e.g., 'to some extent'). Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.

vocabulary.definition: a situation in which you accept less of one thing in order to have more of another

vocabulary.exampleAR: هناك مفاضلة بين التوصيل السريع والأثر البيئي. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: to consider the advantages and disadvantages before making a decision

vocabulary.exampleAR: تعود المرتجعات الفورية غالبًا بتكلفة على البيئة أو ظروف العمال. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: used to soften a claim or show partial agreement

vocabulary.definition: an option that meets needs without compromising the environment or future resources

grammar.concept: Use concessive clauses and qualifiers to acknowledge counterarguments, and combine them with nuanced comparison structures to make balanced evaluations.
grammar.arabicComparison: استخدم جمل القبول وأدوات التأهيل للاعتراف بالحجج المضادة، وادمجها مع تراكيب مقارنة دقيقة لصياغة تقييمات متوازنة.
grammar.structure: Concession: Although + clause, Even if + clause. Qualification: partly/to some extent/somewhat + main clause. Complex comparison: far more + adj + than..., not so much + noun + as + noun, X is no less Y than Z. Example sequence: Although the service is convenient, it is far more expensive than sustainable alternatives to some extent.
grammar.commonError: Dropping the comma after the concessive clause (Although ...), overusing 'but' immediately after 'although', or placing qualifiers in the wrong position (e.g., 'Although partly the service...').
grammar.exampleEN: Although many customers value next-day delivery, it is far more harmful to the environment than less frequent, consolidated shipping; to some extent, convenience obscures hidden costs.
grammar.exampleAR: على الرغم من أن العديد من العملاء يقدرون التوصيل في اليوم التالي، إلا أنه أكثر ضررًا على البيئة بكثير من الشحن الأقل تكرارًا والمركّز؛ إلى حد ما، تختفي التكاليف الخفية وراء السهولة.

readingBrief: Write an original 350–450-word feature article for a city magazine that examines 'the price of convenience'. The piece should open with a short anecdote about a busy parent using multiple delivery services, then present two expert voices (a consumer-rights advocate and a logistics industry representative) who offer contrasting evidence about costs and benefits. Include one small data point (invented is fine) about increased single-use packaging or subscription growth, a short paragraph evaluating social and environmental trade-offs using concession and qualification language, and finish with two practical recommendations: one for individual consumers and one policy suggestion for the city council. Tone: informative but balanced, suitable for educated adult readers. Compare the new context with the earlier lesson and identify one shift in register or evidence.
writingPrompt: Write a 200–260-word letter to the editor of the city magazine in response to the feature 'The price of convenience'. Audience: magazine editor and general readers. Purpose: argue for a specific consumer habit change (for shoppers) and a policy proposal for the city council, while acknowledging valid benefits of convenience. Include at least one concessive clause (start with 'Although' or 'Even if'), one qualifying phrase (e.g., 'to some extent'), and one complex comparison (e.g., 'far more ... than' or 'not so much ... as ...'). Success criteria: formal but accessible register, clear topic sentences, cohesive devices linking evaluation and proposals, and a visible qualification of your main claim. Word count: 200–260 words. Revise the result for a different audience and explain one language choice.

grammar.topic: Advanced modals for obligation, criticism and inference
grammar.arabicName: أزمنة الأفعال المساعدة المتقدمة للالتزام والنقد والاستدلال
grammar.concept: Use modals and semi-modals to: express obligation (must / have to / ought to), issue criticism (shouldn't have / ought not to / needn't have done), and make inferences about past or present situations (must have / may well / might / could). Vary strength: must (strong obligation), should/ought to (advice), may/might (weak inference).
grammar.arabicComparison: لا تُستخدم هذه التركيبات بنفس طريقة العربية دائماً. 'Must' أقوى من 'should'. 'May well' تُستخدم للاستدلال الواثق نسبياً. أمثلة على تركيب الاستنتاج الماضي: 'must have + past participle' = لا بد أن يكون قد...
grammar.structure: Obligation: subject + must / have to / ought to + base verb. Criticism (past): subject + should/ought + have + past participle (for reproach). Inference (present): subject + must / may / might / could + base verb; Inference (past): subject + must / may / might + have + past participle.
grammar.commonError: Using 'must have' for present inference (wrong): 'She must have tired' instead of 'She may be tired' or 'She must be tired.' Confusing strength: avoid mixing 'must' with tentative language when you intend a weak inference.
grammar.exampleEN: Obligation: 'Managers must address harassment reports promptly.' Criticism (past): 'They should have investigated the complaint sooner.' Inference: 'Given the high turnover, morale may well be low.'
grammar.exampleAR: الالتزام: «يجب على المديرين معالجة تقارير التحرش فوراً.» النقد (ماضٍ): «كان يجب عليهم التحقيق في الشكوى في وقت أبكر.» الاستدلال: «بالنظر إلى معدل الدوران العالي، قد تكون المعنويات منخفضة على الأرجح.»

readingBrief: Write a 350–450-word feature article titled 'A workplace worth joining' aimed at a professional business magazine. The piece should combine: (1) a concise narrative opening (a real-feeling anecdote, 2–3 sentences) that introduces a morale issue; (2) two short interview quotes (one from a mid-level manager, one from a junior employee) that show contrasting perspectives; (3) two pieces of evidence (one internal stat such as retention or survey results, one external reference to a sector trend); (4) an evaluation of current policies using advanced modal language (obligation, criticism, inference); (5) a clear recommendation for a pilot initiative (one paragraph) and anticipated objections (brief) with responses. Aim for a balanced, professional tone that models the vocabulary chunks in this lesson. Compare the new context with the earlier lesson and identify one shift in register or evidence.
writingPrompt: Write a 200–260-word formal letter or email to your HR director arguing for a three-month pilot of a flexible-hours policy. Audience: HR director. Purpose: evaluate existing problems, argue for the pilot with two main benefits, acknowledge one likely objection (cost or scheduling), and offer a measurable success criterion. Include a one-sentence counterpoint that qualifies your recommendation (e.g., 'provided that…') and end with a proposed next step. Success criteria: use formal register, include at least two advanced modal forms (one showing obligation or recommendation, one showing inference), use cohesive linking (contrast, cause, concession), and maintain clear paragraphing. Revise the result for a different audience and explain one language choice.

title: When a system fails — Extension 7
