grammar.arabicName: التقرير في المبني للمجهول والبنى غير الشخصية
grammar.concept: Use passive verbs and impersonal constructions to report findings, attribute claims, and present evaluations without overtly personal opinions.
grammar.arabicComparison: استخدم المبني للمجهول والهياكل غير الشخصية لتقديم النتائج ونسب الادعاءات وعرض التقييمات دون التعبير المباشر عن الرأي الشخصي.
grammar.structure: Passive: Subject + be + past participle (e.g. 'The report was published'). Impersonal: 'It was reported that...', 'There is concern that...', 'It was suggested that...'.
grammar.commonError: Students overuse passive to avoid responsibility or mix tenses incorrectly (e.g. 'It is suggested that it happened') or apply 'it was said that' when a named source is available.
grammar.exampleEN: It was concluded that training had been inadequate. The oversight body was asked to investigate further.
grammar.exampleAR: تُوِصل إلى أن التدريب كان غير كافٍ. طُلِب من هيئة الإشراف التحقيق بشكل أعمق.

readingBrief: An original feature (350–450 words) titled 'When a System Fails: who picks up the pieces?' The piece presents a recent local case study (e.g. a medical clinic's records error that left claimants without benefits), summarises evidence from leaked internal emails and an inspection, quotes three stakeholders (an affected resident, a union representative, and a council official), and describes immediate effects plus proposed remedial measures. The text intentionally uses passive reporting and impersonal structures to attribute claims (e.g. 'it was stated that...'), contains a short timeline, and ends with two suggested reforms and an unresolved question about funding. Students will read to identify responsibility, implied criticism, and the language used to distance or assign blame. Compare the new context with the earlier lesson and identify one shift in register or evidence.
writingPrompt: Audience: Local council chief executive and the newspaper's editor. Purpose: In 200–260 words, write a formal letter that (1) evaluates who is responsible for the failure described in the feature, (2) proposes two practical remedial measures, and (3) acknowledges legitimate constraints (for example, budget or legal limits). Include a clear counterpoint or qualification (e.g. 'while immediate compensation is desirable, it may be impractical because...'). Success criteria: use a formal register, include at least two passive or impersonal structures, use six or more target vocabulary items/chunks from this lesson, organise ideas with clear cohesive markers (contrast, cause, proposal), and keep tone persuasive but balanced. Revise the result for a different audience and explain one language choice.

title: The story behind a statistic — Extension 7

outcome.canDo: I can evaluate and explain what a headline statistic actually shows, using hedging, approximations and trend language to make a balanced argument and propose a measured response. Apply the choice to a new B2 context.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع تقييم وشرح ما تكشفه إحصائية عناوين الأخبار، باستخدام عبارات التحفّظ والتقريب ولغة الاتجاه لصياغة حجة متوازنة واقتراح ردٍّ مدروس. طبّق ذلك في سياق جديد من مستوى B2.
outcome.scenario: A local newspaper has published a headline: 'City volunteering up 35% in one year'. Write a short evaluation for the city council newsletter that explains possible reasons for that rise, notes the limits of the data, and proposes one evidence-based action. Your response must consider an alternative explanation and use hedging and approximations.
outcome.scenarioArabic: نشرت صحيفة محلية عنوانًا يقول: «التطوّع في المدينة ارتفع بنسبة 35٪ خلال عام». اكتب تقييمًا قصيرًا لنشرة مجلس المدينة يشرح الأسباب المحتملة لهذا الارتفاع، ويشير إلى حدود البيانات، ويقترح إجراءً واحدًا قائمًا على الأدلة. يجب أن يتضمّن ردّك تفسيرًا منافسًا وأن تستخدم عبارات التحفّظ والتقريب.

retrieval.prompt: Viewpoint (B1 → B2): Recall how you state a simple viewpoint. Now write a 50–60-word paragraph offering two competing viewpoints on why a statistic might have risen, using at least one hedge (may/might) and one approximation (around/about). Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose the B1 skill 'viewpoint' to practise hedging and approximation in a more nuanced B2 evaluation.

retrieval.prompt: Evidence (B1 → B2): List three kinds of evidence (e.g. survey, administrative data, interview) that could support or weaken a headline statistic, and say briefly (one line each) what each kind can and cannot show. Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Make B1 'evidence' more analytical: recognise strengths/limits of different data sources.

retrieval.prompt: Consequence (B1 → B2): Write two short consequence statements (20–30 words each) that show why treating the statistic as definitive could lead to poor policy decisions, using cautious language (e.g. may result in, risk). Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Turn B1 'consequence' into a task requiring hedging and conditional language.

retrieval.prompt: Negotiation (B1 → B2): Imagine you must persuade the council to delay a decision until more data arrive. Draft a 40–50-word persuasive sentence that uses a polite, hedged tone and proposes one compromise. Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Use B1 'negotiation' to practise measured persuasion with hedges and proposals.

network.learningNote: At B2, learners must balance clarity with caution. Use modal verbs (may, might, could), approximators (around, roughly, approximately) and cautious verbs (suggest, appear to, seem to) to avoid overclaiming. Also mention data limits (sample, margin of error, outliers) before proposing actions.
network.learningNoteArabic: في مستوى B2 يجب الموازنة بين الوضوح والتحفّظ. استخدم أفعالًا مُقَيِّدة (may, might, could)، وعبارات تقريب (around, roughly, approximately)، وأفعالًا متحفظة (suggest, appear to, seem to) لتجنّب المبالغة، واذكر حدود البيانات (العينة، هامش الخطأ، القيم الشاذة) قبل اقتراح إجراءات.

wordFamilies.note: Common collocates: analyse data, a quick analysis, in-depth analysis.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: عبارات متكررة: analyse data تحليل البيانات، a quick analysis تحليل سريع، in-depth analysis تحليل عميق.

wordFamilies.note: Estimate is often hedged: we estimate, roughly estimated at, a conservative estimate.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: كلمة estimate غالبًا ما تأتي مع تحفّظ: we estimate نُقدّر، roughly estimated at يُقدّر تقريبًا بـ، a conservative estimate تقدير متحفظ.

wordFamilies.note: Distinguish everyday 'significant' (important) from 'statistical significance' (a technical test).
wordFamilies.noteArabic: ميّز بين 'significant' في المعنى العام (مهم) و'statistical significance' في المعنى الفني (دلالة إحصائية).

vocabulary.definition: used to introduce a factor that affects how you interpret information
vocabulary.exampleEN: In light of the new survey, we should update our assumptions about who uses the service. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: في ضوء الاستطلاع الجديد، ينبغي أن نحدّث افتراضاتنا حول من يستخدم الخدمة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.arabic: يأخذ في الحسبان / يأخذ بعين الاعتبار
vocabulary.definition: to consider something when forming an opinion or making a decision
vocabulary.exampleEN: Planners must take into account seasonal peaks before changing opening hours. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يجب على المخطّطين أن يأخذوا الذُرى الموسمية في الحسبان قبل تغيير ساعات العمل. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: to be caused or motivated mainly by a particular factor
vocabulary.exampleEN: The apparent rise may be driven by a publicity campaign rather than a real change in behaviour. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قد يكون الارتفاع الظاهر مدفوعًا بحملة دعائية بدلاً من تغيير حقيقي في السلوك. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: used to introduce an approximate statement
vocabulary.exampleEN: Roughly speaking, the number doubled between 2023 and 2025. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بشكل تقريبي، تضاعف العدد بين 2023 و2025. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: used to say that something is mainly true
vocabulary.exampleEN: To a large extent, the figures reflect improved reporting rather than more people taking part. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: إلى حد كبير، تعكس الأرقام تحسّن الإبلاغ أكثر من زيادة المشاركين. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: a technical judgement that a result is unlikely to be due to random chance
vocabulary.exampleEN: The report notes that the change lacks statistical significance and could be random variation. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: تشير الدراسة إلى أن التغير يفتقر إلى الدلالة الإحصائية وقد يكون تباينًا عشوائيًا. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: when an observed trend changes direction
vocabulary.exampleEN: After a decade of decline, the city saw a trend reversal in bike use last year. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعد عقد من الانخفاض، شهدت المدينة انعكاسًا في اتجاه استخدام الدراجات العام الماضي. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: a data point that is very different from others and may distort averages
vocabulary.exampleEN: One large donation was an outlier that pushed the average up; median figures tell a different story. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كانت تبرّعًا كبيرًا قيمة شاذة رفعت المتوسط؛ وحكاية الوسيط مختلفة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: an estimate of the range within which the true value is likely to lie
vocabulary.exampleEN: With a margin of error of ±4%, a 6% increase should be treated cautiously. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: مع هامش خطأ ±4٪، يجب التعامل بحذر مع زيادة قدرها 6٪. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: to describe something as greater or more important than it really is
vocabulary.exampleEN: The headline risks overstating the improvement without looking at subgroups. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: العنوان يخاطر بمبالغة التحسّن دون النظر في الفئات الفرعية. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: the distinction between two variables moving together (correlation) and one causing the other (causation)
vocabulary.exampleEN: A correlation between campaign ads and sign-ups does not prove causation; other factors may be involved. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: الترابط بين الإعلانات والتسجيلات لا يثبت السببية؛ قد تكون عوامل أخرى متورطة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: to place information into a broader setting so its meaning becomes clearer
vocabulary.exampleEN: We need to contextualise the figures by presenting monthly breakdowns and local differences. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: نحتاج إلى وضع الأرقام في سياقها من خلال عرض تفصيل شهري والفروقات المحلية. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

grammar.concept: Use modal verbs, approximators and cautious verbs to avoid absolute claims; use verbs and nouns that describe trends (rise, fall, plateau, peak) with time markers and qualifiers.
grammar.arabicComparison: في العربية نستخدم أدوات شرطية وأحوال ظرفية للتخفيف، لكن في الإنجليزية الاعتماد الأكبر يكون على أفعال مساعدة (may, might) وعبارات تقريب (around, roughly) وكذلك أفعال وصف الاتجاه (increase, plateau).
grammar.structure: Modal hedges: may/might/could + verb; cautious verbs: appear to / seem to / suggest; approximators: around/about/roughly/approximately + number; trend language: increase/decrease/peak/plateau + time phrase; add qualifiers: to a large extent / partly / largely.
grammar.commonError: Using absolute verbs (prove, confirm) or exact numbers without acknowledging uncertainty; confusing correlation with causation.
grammar.exampleEN: The figure may partly reflect improved reporting rather than an actual rise; roughly speaking, registrations increased by about 30% between 2023 and 2025.
grammar.exampleAR: قد يعكس الرقم جزئيًا تحسّن الإبلاغ بدلًا من ارتفاع حقيقي؛ وبشكل تقريبي، زادت التسجيلات بنحو 30٪ بين 2023 و2025.

readingBrief: Students will read an original 350–450-word feature titled 'The story behind the 24% rise in recorded homelessness'. The piece combines a clear headline statistic with: a breakdown of the data sources (street counts, shelter registrations), a council official's quote, a local charity's perspective, notes on a possible change in counting methods, mention of margin of error and one outlier month, and at least two hedged interpretations (may/might, around/approximately). Learners must identify hedges and approximations, note where the author draws conclusions without sufficient evidence, and prepare a short critique (80–100 words) assessing whether the article justifies the headline. Compare the new context with the earlier lesson and identify one shift in register or evidence.
writingPrompt: Write 200–260 words for the city council newsletter (audience: council officers and informed residents). Purpose: evaluate the headline claim 'Volunteering up 35% in a year' from a recent report, explain two plausible explanations (one you favour, one counterpoint), note one limitation of the data (e.g. margin of error or outlier), and propose one practical, evidence-based action the council could take. You must: use a formal but measured register; include at least two hedges (may/might/could) and one approximation (around/about/roughly); qualify your recommendation (e.g. conditional on further data); and link ideas with clear cohesion devices (e.g. In light of..., however..., therefore...). Success criteria: 1) Appropriate formal register for officials and residents; 2) Use of hedging and approximation to avoid overclaiming; 3) Logical cohesion with clear contrast and conclusion; 4) 200–260 words. Revise the result for a different audience and explain one language choice.

title: A difficult decision — Extension 7

outcome.canDo: I can evaluate an ethical dilemma, argue for a justified course of action, and propose a solution that anticipates consequences using mixed conditionals and counterfactual reasoning. Apply the choice to a new B2 context.
outcome.canDoArabic: أستطيع تقييم مأزق أخلاقي، والجدال لصالح حل مبرر، واقتراح حل يتوقع العواقب باستخدام الشروط المختلطة والتفكير الافتراضي. طبّق ذلك في سياق جديد من مستوى B2.
outcome.scenario: You are writing to the editor of a community newsletter after a local charity decided to cancel a long-running programme because of budget cuts. Some residents praise the decision; others call it irresponsible. Argue your position, evaluate the consequences for different groups, and propose a revised plan that balances ethics and finances.
outcome.scenarioArabic: أنت تكتب إلى محرر نشرة مجتمعية بعد أن ألغت جمعية خيرية محلية برنامجًا طويل الأمد بسبب خفض الميزانية. بعض السكان يثنون على القرار؛ وآخرون يعتبرونه غير مسؤول. جدل موقفك، قيّم العواقب على مجموعات مختلفة، واقتراح خطة معدلة توازن بين الأخلاق والمالية.

retrieval.prompt: Recall a recent time you had to change your viewpoint. Briefly narrate the situation (3–4 sentences) and list two pieces of evidence that changed your opinion. Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Activate B1 narrative + viewpoint skills and prepare specific evidence for B2 evaluation.

retrieval.prompt: اذكر موقفًا اضطررت فيه إلى إعادة ترتيب أولوياتك. اكتب سردًا موجزًا (3–4 جمل) وحدد نتيجة أو عاقبة واحدة ظهرت لاحقًا. Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: إعادة استخدام مهارات B1 (consequence/أثر) للتحضير لمناقشة عواقب القرار.

retrieval.prompt: Describe one negotiation you took part in and explain which two concessions were made. Which concession had the greater long-term cost? Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: Repurpose B1 negotiation into analysis of short- versus long-term consequences.

retrieval.prompt: صف موقفًا قدمت فيه دليلاً ليقنع شخصًا ما بتغيير رأيه. ما الدليل الأقوى؟ قل جملة واحدة تبرز لماذا كان هذا الدليل مقنعًا. Reconnect it to this B2 lesson.
retrieval.purpose: تحويل مهارة B1 (evidence/دليل) إلى مهمة لتقييم قوة الدليل.

network.anchor: If the charity had considered smaller cuts, it would still be supporting the vulnerable now — mixed conditionals help explain past choices and present consequences.
network.learningNote: Mixed conditionals let you link a different-time cause and effect: 'If + past perfect' with 'would + base' talks about present results of past events; 'If + past' with 'would have + past participle' talks about past results of present or continuing unreal situations. Use them to evaluate how an earlier choice affects current reality.
network.learningNoteArabic: الشروط المختلطة تربط سببًا ونتيجة في زمنين مختلفين: 'if + الماضي التام' مع 'would + المصدر' لتوضيح نتائج حالية لحدث ماضٍ؛ و'if + الماضي البسيط' مع 'would have + التصريف الثالث' لتوضيح نتائج ماضية لو كانت الحالة الحالية مختلفة. استخدمها لتقييم كيف يؤثر قرار سابق على الواقع الحالي.

wordFamilies.note: Use 'consequence' for outcomes; 'consequential' for something important or resulting from something; 'consequently' links cause and effect in formal writing.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: 'consequence' لِـ 'نتيجة'؛ 'consequential' بمعنى مُهِمّ أو ناجم عن؛ 'consequently' تربط السبب والنتيجة في اللغة الرسمية.

wordFamilies.note: Use verbs and nouns to talk about ordering tasks or resources; 'prioritisation' is useful in formal proposals.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: استخدم الفعل والاسم للحديث عن ترتيب المهام أو الموارد؛ 'prioritisation' مناسبة في الاقتراحات الرسمية.

wordFamilies.note: As a verb, 'compromise' = make concessions; as a noun, it is the result. 'Compromising' describes actions that reduce standards or integrity.
wordFamilies.noteArabic: كفعل: تقديم تنازلات؛ كاسم: نتيجة تلك التنازلات. 'compromising' تصف أفعالًا قد تضعف المعايير.

vocabulary.definition: a situation where you must choose between two morally important but conflicting options
vocabulary.exampleEN: The trustees faced an ethical dilemma: close the day centre or cut vital staff support. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: واجه الأمناء مأزقًا أخلاقيًا: إغلاق المركز النهاري أم تقليص دعم الموظفين الحيوي. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: to carefully consider the possible results of an action before deciding
vocabulary.exampleEN: Before reducing services, the council should weigh the consequences for elderly residents. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قبل تقليص الخدمات، ينبغي للمجلس موازنة العواقب على السكان المسنين. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: to accept that you are the cause of something or must deal with its results
vocabulary.exampleEN: The director had to take responsibility for the programme's cancellation in public statements. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كان على المدير أن يتحمل مسؤولية إلغاء البرنامج في التصريحات العلنية. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: considering the longer future rather than immediate effects
vocabulary.exampleEN: Cutting preventive services may save money now but cost more in the long run. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: قد توفر تقليص الخدمات الوقائية المال الآن لكنها تكلف أكثر على المدى الطويل. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: a systematic calculation of advantages and disadvantages of different options
vocabulary.exampleEN: A thorough cost–benefit analysis revealed that a smaller programme could continue with volunteer support. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كشف تحليل التكلفة والفائدة الشامل أن برنامجًا أصغر يمكن أن يستمر بدعم المتطوعين. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: used to introduce consideration of the risks, consequences or importance of a situation when deciding or judging an action.
vocabulary.exampleEN: If the committee had realised how severely people would be affected, given the stakes they would not be implementing the policy now. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: لو أن اللجنة أدركت مدى تأثُّر الناس بشدّة، لما كانت ستنفّذ السياسة الآن، نظراً لما هو على المحك. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: a duty based on ethical principles rather than legal requirement
vocabulary.exampleEN: Many volunteers felt a moral obligation to continue supporting the service. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: شعر العديد من المتطوعين بالتزام أخلاقي بمواصلة دعم الخدمة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: to accept the unpleasant consequences of one's actions
vocabulary.exampleEN: After the budget leak, the manager had to face the music in a public meeting. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: بعد تسريب الميزانية، اضطر المدير إلى مواجهة العواقب في اجتماع علني. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: to make something less severe or harmful
vocabulary.exampleEN: We can mitigate the impact on users by offering alternative services. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: يمكننا تخفيف التأثير على المستخدمين بتقديم خدمات بديلة. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: to put tasks or causes in order of importance
vocabulary.exampleEN: The charity must prioritise essential services over discretionary projects. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: على الجمعية أن تُعطي الأولوية للخدمات الأساسية على المشاريع الاختيارية. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: a consequence, especially one that causes complications
vocabulary.exampleEN: The policy change had unexpected legal ramifications for tenants. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: كان لتغيير السياسة تداعيات قانونية غير متوقعة على المستأجرين. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

vocabulary.definition: to accept less than full demands in order to reach agreement; an agreement reached by mutual concession
vocabulary.exampleEN: They compromised by reducing opening hours rather than closing entirely. Use it again in a fresh B2 situation.
vocabulary.exampleAR: توصلوا إلى حل وسط بتقليل ساعات العمل بدلًا من الإغلاق الكامل. استخدمها مرة أخرى في موقف جديد من مستوى B2.

grammar.concept: Use mixed conditionals to link a hypothetical past cause with a present result or a hypothetical present cause with a past result. This lets you express how different choices would change current realities or past outcomes.
grammar.arabicComparison: تربط الشروط المختلطة سببا افتراضيا في الماضي بنتيجة حالية، أو سبب افتراضيا في الحاضر بنتيجة ماضية.
grammar.structure: If + past perfect, would + base (present result of past cause). / If + past simple, would have + past participle (past result of present/unreal cause).
grammar.commonError: Mixing forms incorrectly (e.g. 'If we had cut costs, we would have less funding now' — incorrect pairing of times). Watch that the verb forms match the intended time relationship.
grammar.exampleEN: If the board had consulted residents, they would be less angry now. / If the charity were more transparent, it would have avoided the recent backlash.
grammar.exampleAR: لو أن المجلس استشار السكان لكانوا أقل غضبًا الآن. / لو أن الجمعية كانت أكثر شفافية، لكانت تجنبت رد الفعل الأخير.

readingBrief: Read an original 350–450-word feature article that reports on a recent local charity decision to cancel a community health programme. The feature includes: (a) an account of the decision and the stated financial reasons; (b) short interviews with two affected people (a beneficiary and a volunteer); (c) an analysis section that uses counterfactual statements and mixed conditionals to consider alternative choices and their likely present consequences; and (d) a brief summary of proposed compromises. The author takes a balanced stance and invites readers to consider both ethical obligations and budgetary realities. Compare the new context with the earlier lesson and identify one shift in register or evidence.
writingPrompt: Write a 200–260-word letter to the editor of the community newsletter arguing for a revised plan. Audience: local residents and decision-makers. Purpose: evaluate the charity's decision, propose a feasible compromise, and anticipate likely consequences. Include at least two mixed conditional sentences (one linking a past choice to a present situation, and one linking a present hypothetical to a past outcome). Address a counterpoint (e.g., limited funds) and qualify your recommendation accordingly. Success criteria: formal but accessible register; clear topic sentences; at least three target chunks from the lesson; logical cohesion (use of connectors and at least two mixed conditionals); and persuasive, evidence-based reasoning. Revise the result for a different audience and explain one language choice.
